content.value_statement: CI failures can hide the first useful error among checks, logs, and repeated noise. This skill gathers relevant GitHub evidence and produces a prioritized plan for repair.
actual_capabilities: Inspect pull request checks and identify failed workflows with GitHub CLI.
Retrieve and organize relevant CI job logs and error messages.
Group failures by formatting, linting, tests, builds, and platform.
Create a concise repair plan with affected checks and suggested follow-up skills.
Recommend verification steps after fixes are applied.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI with access to the repository and workflow logs.
Diagnoses available evidence but does not implement code fixes automatically.
Cannot recover logs that GitHub has expired or that permissions hide.
Recommendations depend on the workflow names, log quality, and repository context.

use_cases.title: Triage a pull request
use_cases.description: Review failing checks on an active pull request and isolate the earliest actionable error.

use_cases.title: Prepare a repair handoff
use_cases.description: Convert noisy CI output into a prioritized plan that another engineer can implement.

use_cases.title: Investigate cross-platform failures
use_cases.description: Compare platform-specific checks and identify whether formatting, tests, builds, or tooling cause the failure.

prompt_templates.title: Check my pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the CI status for pull request <number> in <owner>/<repo>. Summarize failed checks and the first useful error for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: get a concise status summary.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the failing logs
prompt_templates.prompt: For pull request <number>, retrieve the relevant failed job logs, remove repeated noise, and explain the likely cause in plain language.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: understand the evidence behind a failure.

prompt_templates.title: Build a fix plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all failed checks for pull request <number>. Group related failures, rank them by likely root cause, and create a step-by-step repair plan with verification commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: turn diagnosis into implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Compare platform failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate pull request <number> across macOS, Linux, and Windows checks. Distinguish shared root causes from platform-specific issues and cite the evidence for each conclusion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: analyze a multi-platform CI incident.

output_examples.input: Diagnose the failures on pull request 42.
output_examples.output: The Linux test job fails first because a fixture is missing. Formatting and downstream build checks may be secondary failures. Recommended order: restore the fixture, rerun tests, then address formatting.

output_examples.input: Compare the failed macOS and Linux checks.
output: Both platforms report the same dependency resolution error.
The Windows job passed, so the issue may depend on runner configuration or lockfile handling.
Verify the dependency cache and lockfile before changing application code.

best_practices: Provide the repository and pull request number so the diagnosis targets the correct checks.
Fix the earliest root-cause failure before addressing downstream or repeated errors.
Review the proposed commands and changes before running them in a repository.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every failed check as an independent root cause.
Do not expose private logs or credentials in copied prompts or issue comments.
Do not rerun expensive workflows repeatedly without changing the suspected cause.

faq.question: What does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects pull request checks, failed workflow jobs, and accessible GitHub Actions logs.

faq.question: Does it fix the code?
faq.answer: No. It explains the evidence and prepares a repair plan for an engineer to review and implement.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: The GitHub CLI must be authenticated and authorized to read the repository and relevant workflow logs.

faq.question: Can it diagnose local test failures?
faq.answer: It focuses on CI evidence. You can provide local output separately, but local execution is not its primary capability.

faq.question: How does it handle many failures?
faq.answer: It groups related checks and prioritizes likely root causes before secondary failures.

faq.question: Should I run suggested commands immediately?
faq.answer: No. Review each command, its scope, and its repository impact before execution.
